title: Service management
subtitle: init.d scripts and systemd units — flip for meaning, example, and notes

cards.meaning: init.d = a shell script per service; systemd = declarative unit file + systemctl
cards.notes: Modern Linux defaults to systemd; many boxes still accept legacy init.d scripts for compatibility.

cards.meaning: SysV script API: start, stop, or restart that service
cards.notes: Also reload and force-reload. On some systems service nginx start wraps the same scripts. The file is a case on $1.
Memory hook: init.d start|stop|restart → systemctl start|stop|restart. Add status, enable, daemon-reload.

cards.meaning: enable = start at boot; disable = do not start at boot
cards.notes: Uses [Install] WantedBy=. start/stop = now; enable/disable = boot.

cards.meaning: Reload unit files after you edit one
cards.notes: Required so systemd re-reads the changed unit before restart picks up new settings.

cards.meaning: status = running? recent logs?; is-active = exit 0 if active
cards.notes: Everyday checks before and after start/stop/restart.
Vendor = /usr/lib/systemd/system/. You customize or add = /etc/systemd/system/. Runtime = /run/systemd/system/.

cards.meaning: Who I wait for · how I run · which target enables me
Wants = weak dep (start them, need not succeed); Requires = strong (if they fail, this fails)
cards.notes: Wants is polite; Requires is strict. Also Before=/After= for ordering only.

cards.meaning: When enabled, this unit is pulled in by the normal server boot target
cards.notes: Targets (.target) replace SysV runlevels. Servers typically want multi-user.target.

cards.meaning: Start script daemonizes: parent exits, child stays
cards.notes: Often paired with PIDFile=. Other types: simple, oneshot, notify, …

cards.meaning: Command that starts / stops the supervised process
Reload config if the unit supports it (without a full stop)
cards.notes: Parallel to /etc/init.d/nginx reload. Not every unit implements reload.

cards.meaning: List all service units, even inactive ones
cards.notes: Useful inventory when hunting what is installed vs running.

cards.meaning: Daemons · cron-like schedules · boot stages · socket activation
cards.notes: Also device, mount, path, slice, scope. Full keys: man systemd.unit.
